questions.question_text: Compare and contrast Imperative programming and Declarative Programming.
What is data encapsulation, and why is it useful?
questions.answer: Encapsulation is a concept in Object-Oriented Programming for combining properties and methods in a single unit. Encapsulation helps developers follow a modular approach for software development because each object has its own set of methods and variables and serves its functions independent of other objects. In addition to that, encapsulation serves data hiding purposes.

questions.question_text: Differentiate Concurrent and Parallel programming with example.
questions.answer:
Concurrent Programming:
Refers to the concept where multiple tasks or processes progress simultaneously in overlapping time periods. These tasks may not actually be running at the same time but are managed in such a way that they appear to be executing concurrently by interleaving steps. The focus is on task structure and responsiveness, even if not all tasks run simultaneously.

Parallel Programming:
In parallel programming, multiple tasks are executed simultaneously across multiple cores or processors. The tasks truly run at the same time. The focus is on dividing a large task into smaller subtasks that can be executed simultaneously for better performance.

questions.question_text: Discuss about Böhm-Jacopini theorem with suitable example?
questions.answer:
The Böhm-Jacopini theorem states that any algorithm can be written using only three basic control structures:
1. Sequence: Executing statements one after another.
2. Selection: Making decisions, typically represented by if-else statements or switch cases.
3. Iteration: Repeating tasks, often represented by while, for, or do-while loops.

A newly constructed University is going to manage book details in the library where each book has a title, author, ISBN number, and the number of copies available. They are in the need of computer software which is going to manage libray for easy management of book. You are requested to design a Book class with fields for title, author, ISBN, and copiesAvailable. Create a constructor to initialize these fields. Write a method displayBookInfo() to display the book's detail and also write a method addbookToLibrary() to additon of books.

A company has different types of employees such as full-time and part-time employees. Full-time employees have a fixed salary, while part-time employees are paid by the hour. Create a superclass Employee with fields name, employeeId, and department. Create two subclasses: FullTimeEmployee (with a field fixedSalary) and PartTimeEmployee (with fields hourlyWage and hoursWorked). Implement methods in the subclasses to calculate the salary for each type of employee. Create a method in the Employee superclass called displayEmployeeDetails() and override it in both subclasses to display specific details for full-time and part-time employees. Discuss how method overriding works in inheritance.

A vehicle rental company offers various types of vehicles, such as cars, trucks, and bikes. Each vehicle type has a different way of calculating rental costs. Create an interface Rentable with methods rent() and calculateRentalCost(int days). Implement this interface in classes Car, Truck, and Bike, where each class provides its own method of calculating rental costs. Create an abstract class Vehicle that implements the Rentable interface and provides common properties like make, model, and year. Extend this abstract class in the Car, Truck, and Bike classes. Discuss how abstraction allows for code reuse.

You are working on a zoo simulation program. There are different animals such as Lion, Elephant, and Bird. Each animal can makeSound(), but the sound they make is different for each animal. You are requested to create a base class Animal with a method makeSound(). Implement subclasses Lion, Elephant, and Bird, overriding the makeSound() method in each. Write a program that demonstrates how polymorphism can be used to make each animal produce its respective sound by calling makeSound() on an Animal reference.
